budget_bytes.description: The size the cache may grow to when disk space allows.

DictionaryDefinitions.description: One dictionary's entry for a result, with the meaning of each tag it uses.

DictionaryPronunciation.description: A pitch accent or IPA transcription from one dictionary.

DictionaryStylesheet.description:
The CSS that a dictionary ships for its own entries, unsanitized.
Displays must sanitize it and confine it to that dictionary's entries before applying it.

source_language.description: The language of the words looked up, as a BCP 47 tag, when the dictionary states it.

target_language.description: The language of the definitions, as a BCP 47 tag, when the dictionary states it.

cue_index.description: The index of the subtitle cue the card was made from, when it was made from one.

included_fields.description: The fields the card shows, in no particular order.

oneOf.description: The media file the card was made from. Null once that file has been removed from the project.

FlashcardContent.description: Everything a flashcard can hold. L1 is the language the user already knows; L2 is the one they are learning.

FlashcardDraft.description: What the editor sends to create or replace a flashcard.

FlashcardFieldKey.description: The fields of a flashcard, named as the keys of `FlashcardContent`.

Frequency.description: How common a term is. The dictionary's `FrequencyMode` says whether higher values mean more or less common.

display.description: The text to show in place of the value, if the dictionary gives one.

value.description: The number to sort by, if the dictionary gives one.

path.description:

A CSV, TSV or Tabfile table file is imported on its own.

oneOf.description: Replaces the detected layout of a CSV, TSV or Tabfile table.

KanjiEntry.description: A single kanji character with its readings and meanings.

kunyomi.description: Native Japanese readings, written in hiragana.

onyomi.description: Readings borrowed from Chinese, written in katakana.

stats.description: Facts such as stroke count or grade, keyed by the name of the tag that labels them.

KanjiResult.description: One dictionary's entry for a single kanji character.

kanji.description: The kanji dictionary entries for the first character, when it is a kanji.

results.description: The terms that the text may begin with, best first.

stylesheets.description: The stylesheets of the dictionaries whose definitions appear in `results`, each once.

LookupResult.description: The entries of every dictionary for one term and reading that the looked-up text may stand for.

inflectionChains.description:
The equally good chains of inflections that lead from the term to the matched text, the most plausible first.
Each chain names its inflections outermost first. The list is empty when no inflection was undone.

matchedText.description: The beginning of the looked-up text that this result covers.

oneOf.description:
The finite verb and the particle, with their places in the context, when the term is a particle verb
whose parts stand apart, as rufe and an in „Ich rufe dich morgen an".

so it records only what identifies the file when the user picks it again.

ParseTimedTextRequest.description: The request body shared by the HTTP route and the WebAssembly facade.

PitchAccent.description: The pitch accent of one reading of a Japanese term.

devoice.description: Mora positions, counted from 1, that are devoiced.

nasal.description: Mora positions, counted from 1, that are pronounced nasally.

One letter per mora, `H` for high and `L` for low, optionally followed by one letter for a following particle.

PlaybackEngine.description: The browser engine behind the media element, decided from the user agent.

can_play_type.description: The answer to `canPlayType` for the file's direct MIME type with codecs.

mse_codec_strings.description: The RFC 6381 codec strings that `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` accepts in fragmented MP4.

oneOf.description: The client plays the file's own bytes in a media element.

allOf.description: The server converts the file into HLS with fragmented MP4 segments while it plays.

Project.description: A project with its settings and the counts the home screen shows.

last_opened_at_ms.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Equal to `created_at_ms` until the project is first opened.

ProjectSettings.description: Everything a user sets about a project, as the project form edits it.

fills_audio_with_tts.description: Whether the audio fields are filled with text-to-speech when the media has no audio track.

flashcard_fields.description: The fields a new flashcard starts with.

tags_media_name.description: Whether each new flashcard is also tagged with the name of the media file it was made from.

target_language.description: The language being learned, as a BCP 47 code.

translation_language.description: The language translations and definitions are in, as a BCP 47 code.

Rational.description: A positive ratio of two integers, such as a timebase of `1/90000` or a frame rate of `30000/1001`.

Screenshot.description: A still frame of the video, named by the time it is taken at. The image itself is read from the media file.

SeparatedVerb.description: A particle verb whose finite verb and particle stand apart, as rufe and an in „Ich rufe dich morgen an".

SubtitleRole.description: Which role a subtitle track plays for its media file.

SubtitleSelection.description: The subtitle tracks a media file shows: one in the language being learned, one translation.

SubtitleTrack.description: A subtitles file added to a media file. Its cues are read through their own route.

name.description: The name shown in the track list, usually the file name.

sample.description: The text of the first cue, for telling tracks apart.

TableLayout.description: What each column of a table holds, and whether its first row is a header.

TablePreview.description: The layout detected in a table, with its first rows, for a person to check before importing.

rows.description: The first rows of the table, including any header row, split into cells.

TagDefinition.description: The meaning of a tag that a dictionary attaches to its entries.

category.description: A grouping such as `partOfSpeech` or `frequent`, which display uses to color the tag.

notes.description: A longer description of the tag.

order.description: The position of the tag among others; lower comes first.

TermEntry.description: One headword of a dictionary with its definitions.

alternates.description: Other spellings under which the entry is found, such as StarDict synonyms or MDict redirects.

reading.description: How the term is read, for scripts such as kanji where the spelling does not show it.

score.description: The dictionary's own ranking among entries with the same headword; higher comes first.

sequence.description: An identifier shared by entries that the dictionary treats as one word.

wordClasses.description: The inflection classes of the term, such as `v1` or `adj-i`, which deinflection matches against.

TextSource.description:
Where the text of a request comes from.

The `path` variant names a file on the machine running the server. The server resolves
it, and only for requests authenticated with the per-launch token. The WebAssembly build
supports only the `inline` variant.

TrackInfo.description: One stream inside a container. Fields the source does not state are `None`.

codec.description: ffmpeg's name for the codec, such as `h264`, `aac`, or `subrip`.

codec_string.description:
The RFC 6381 codec string in the spelling Media Source Extensions accept,
or `None` when the codec cannot be carried in fragmented MP4.

container_track_id.description:
The identifier the container itself uses for the track, such as the MP4 track id
or the Matroska track number, when known.

index.description: The stream's position counted over all stream kinds, as in ffmpeg's `0:N`.

language.description: The language tag stored in the container, or `None` when it is undetermined.

profile.description: ffmpeg's name for the codec profile, such as `High` or `LC`.

direct_mime_type.description:
The MIME type with codecs to pass to `canPlayType`, or `None` when the file's own bytes
cannot play in a media element at all.

oneOf.description: Transcode to H.264, scaled to `scale_to` when set, at `bit_rate` bits per second.

WaveformResponse.description:
One window of waveform peaks: 100 per second from `start_ms`, each the loudest sample of the
loudest channel in its hundredth of a second, from 0 (silence) to 255 (full scale).
